description: A cooperative Texas Hold'em ranking game. Pick chips to communicate hand strength and complete heists together.

actionLog.takeChip: Player {{player}} chooses the {{chip}}★ chip in round {{round}}
actionLog.endRound: Player {{player}} ends round {{round}} and advances to round {{nextRound}}

steps.intro: Win three heists before the team trips three alarms. Each round starts with your two pocket cards, then you use chips to signal where you think your hand ranks.
steps.goalTrack: This shows the current heist plus gold and alarm progress. Three gold bars win the game; three alarms lose it.
steps.hand: These are your pocket cards and current best hand. You cannot state your cards, so read your hand, the table cards, and the chips other players have taken.
steps.handRankReference: The Hands button in the lower-left is the in-game quick reference. Keep it closed most of the time; open it only when you need to confirm the weak-to-strong order before choosing chips or reading showdown.
steps.startHeist: This heist has not officially started yet. The host starts it from the lower-right action button; after that, expansion settings lock and players can take chips.
steps.chipChoice: Choose an available white chip. A higher number says you think your hand is stronger; a lower number leaves stronger positions for teammates.
steps.tableResponse: Your teammates take white chips too. The center pool is the default source, but current-round white chips in front of teammates are also legal targets; taking one rewrites this round's public strength signal. Only chips are public for now, not hands.
steps.takePlayerChip: Try it now: click the glowing current-round white chip in front of a teammate and take it from them. That player loses the chip, then the AI will choose another available chip. You may still keep only one chip of each color yourself.
steps.advanceRound: When everyone has a chip, advance the round. Advancing waits for every player to confirm; AI seats confirm automatically. Community cards will appear and everyone reassesses their hand strength.
steps.communityCards: Community cards can change your best hand. Later rounds add the turn and river, and each round asks for a new chip color.
steps.yellowChip: Reassess your hand strength and take a yellow chip. Yellow chips revise the strength signal from the white chips.
steps.yellowResponse: Your teammates take yellow chips too. Comparing white and yellow chips shows who thinks the community cards helped them.
steps.turnRound: When all yellow chips are chosen, everyone confirms before advancing to the turn. The next community card can change the ranking again.
steps.turnCard: The turn card is out. With four community cards on the table, reassess the order again.
steps.orangeChip: Take an orange chip for the third-round judgment. By now, everyone has three public signals to calibrate against.
steps.orangeResponse: Your teammates take orange chips too. Remember how each player moved from white to orange before red chips lock the final order.
steps.riverRound: When all orange chips are chosen, everyone confirms before advancing to the river. The fifth community card leads into the final commitment.
steps.finalChip: The red chip is the final commitment. Read your two pocket cards with all five community cards before choosing your final rank.
steps.finalResponse: Your teammates take red chips too. The three red chips form the final strength order that showdown will check.
steps.revealShowdown: After all red chips are chosen, reveal showdown. Showdown also waits for every player to confirm; AI seats confirm automatically. The game compares real hand order against the red chip order.
steps.showdown: Showdown keeps the five already-public community cards visible, then reveals each player's two pocket cards, red chip, hand category, and whether the heist succeeded. With more players, scroll down to review everyone's real cards instead of squeezing the settlement into one screen.
steps.showdownReading: Read showdown by checking the community cards, then scrolling through each player's two pocket cards and hand category before comparing those hands with the red chips. Stronger real hands should have higher red-chip numbers; if any red-chip order disagrees with real hand strength, the heist fails.
steps.finish: The loop is: read hand strength, signal rank with chips, reassess as public cards appear, lock final order with red chips, then resolve showdown.

board.handRankListAria: Quick list of hands from weakest to strongest
board.rulesDialogHostHint: Before the heist starts, the host can freely combine modes and challenges. Settings lock once the heist is underway.
board.rulesDialogLockedHostHint: You are the host, but this heist has already started; expansion rules are view-only now.
board.rulesDialogGuestHint: Only the host can change setup rules right now; you can still review the active mode and challenges.
board.rulesDialogSource: Based on the TTS mode button, challenge zone, and info board
board.rulesLocked: This heist has started; expansion settings are locked
board.toastStartBeforeChip: The host must start the heist before chips can be taken.
board.toastRulesLocked: This heist has started; expansion settings can no longer be changed.
board.toastHostOnlySetup: Only the host can change setup rules.
board.toastHostOnlyStart: Only the host can start the heist.

board.toastToolsAlreadyDealt: Tool cards have already been dealt for this heist.

gameModeDescriptions.texas-holdem: Standard 2-card hand plus shared board, compatible with the broadest challenge set.
gameModeDescriptions.seven-card-stud: No shared board; each player gets 3 hand cards and personal face-up cards in later rounds.
gameModeDescriptions.banana-split: Neighboring players share face-up columns for a more complex information puzzle.

ttsSetupOptionDescriptions.omaha: Each hand gets 2 extra cards; showdown must use exactly 2 hand cards and 3 board cards.
ttsSetupOptionDescriptions.twoHand: Each player receives top and bottom hands. Showdown evaluates both and uses the stronger hand for ranking. Up to 5 players.
ttsSetupOptionDescriptions.handSwap: After 2Hand is enabled, each completed chip vote opens a swap stage where top and bottom hands may exchange 1 card each.
ttsSetupOptionDescriptions.automode: Automatically advances after all players take chips; the final chip round automatically reveals showdown.
ttsSetupOptionDescriptions.antiTroll: Matches the TTS anti-misclick/host-clearance toggle; Web setup remains host-gated.

exitChipModeDescriptions.default: Default: exit chips appear from 7 players upward, scaling with player count.
exitChipModeDescriptions.mastermind: Mastermind: one fewer exit chip than default.
exitChipModeDescriptions.mega-mastermind: Mega Mastermind: two fewer exit chips than default.

exitChipModeSummaries.default: Uses the TTS default exit chip count.
exitChipModeSummaries.mastermind: One fewer exit chip than default.
exitChipModeSummaries.mega-mastermind: Two fewer exit chips than default.
exitChipModeSummaries.ultra-mastermind: Exit chip count is reduced to 0.

board.toolsReadyToDealStatus: Host action: deal 1 random tool to each player.
board.toolsGuestStatus: Only the host can deal or reset tool cards.
board.toolsDealtStatus: Tool cards have been dealt to {{players}} players; usable cards are marked as usable.
board.nightVisionPickerHint: Choose one hand card to place on Night Vision Goggles. It leaves your hand area but still counts at showdown.
board.chooseNightVisionCard: Choose hand card {{index}} {{card}} for Night Vision Goggles

endgame.winSubtitle: The Gang closed three cases and everyone wins together.
endgame.loseSubtitle: The alarms reached three, and The Gang did not make it out cleanly.
